groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
W: Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such short notice.
M: Not a problem, Margaret. Now, please give me some good news. Have you agreed to my last proposal?
W: I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract.
M: Margaret, we've been through this for almost a year now, back and forth, making alterations. Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients, or not? I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.
W: I understand your concerns. But as I'm sure you understand, we hold our clients' best interests to be of the utmost concern. We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts, rest assured, we all appreciate your firm's patience.
M: OK, fine. So what change do you wish to make?
W: Essentially, we would like the new deal to exclude the Middle East. That's all.
M: The Middle East? Why?
W: My client has a couple of other prospective marketing deals from companies in the Middle East. Those offers, should they materialize, would exclusively employ my client's image in the Middle East only. Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.
M: What business sector in the Middle East are we talking about here?
W: Real estate.
M: Well, that should be okay then. So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market, there should be no conflict of interest. Nevertheless, I will have to run this through my people. I don't foresee any problem, though. The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: Next, we have a special science-related news story. Paula Hancocks at the Denver Observatory. Paula, what is the big story over there?
W: Hi, John. Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited. In fact, space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky.
M: Why? What's the big event? Is there an eclipse happening soon?
W: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet. It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years. For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object.
M: How far away is this comet? Will people be able to see it with the naked eye?
W: The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy. But nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope. People will only see a blur without one. However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment. Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object.
M: Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once-in-a-lifetime event. Where will this comet be in the sky? How can people find it?
W: The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator. However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky. And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.
M: How fantastic! Thank you, Paula, for the information.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world. While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods?
Two papers published today in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of ultra-processed foods to help inform dietary guidelines beyond conventional food classification systems. The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of São Paulo and Arne Astrup of Novo Nordisk Foundation, will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate August 14th during NUTRITION 2024 LIVE ONLINE.
The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed. The system defines ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product. Ultra-processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty, and convenient; examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready-to-heat products, and reconstituted meat products.
Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods—which are packed high in salt, sugar, and fat—with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet. While the mechanisms behind these associations are not fully understood, Monteiro argues that the existing evidence is sufficient to justify discouraging consumption of ultra-processed foods in dietary recommendations and government policies.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
Believe it or not, human creativity benefits from constraints. According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently. With constraints, you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully. When challenged, you figure out new ways to be better.
The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher. People who invent new products are not limited by what they don't have or can't do. They leverage their limitations to push themselves even further. Many products and services are created because the founders saw a limitation in what they use. They created innovation based on what was not working for them at the moment.
Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation. In a 2015 study which examined how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources, Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways. When people face scarcity, they give themselves the freedom to use resources in less conventional ways because they have to. Obstacles can broaden your perception and open up your thinking processes. Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
Marissa Mayer, former vice president for search products and user experience at Google, once wrote in a publication on Bloomberg, "Constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome; Creativity thrives best when constrained."

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts. These strategies are learned in childhood. Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations. We just do whatever seems to come naturally. But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts. When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person. How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict. Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified.
The turtle. Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts. They give up their personal goals and relationships. They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it.
The shark. Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict. They seek to achieve their goals at all costs. Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing. Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement. Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy, and failure.
The teddy bear. Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people. They think that conflict should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships. They give up their goals to preserve the relationship.
The fox. Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people. They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals. They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
The owl. Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved. They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people. They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem. By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship. Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person's goals, and they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health. Scientists hope that cracking the genetic code of plants and animals could help uncover new treatments for infectious diseases, slow aging, improve crops in agriculture, and create new bio-materials.
In Britain, organizations including the Natural History Museum, the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew and the Wellcome Sanger Institute have joined forces to sequence Britain's 66,000 species of animals and plants. Dubbed the Darwin Tree of Life Project, it is expected to take 10 years and cost £100 million. Once completed, all the information will be publicly available to researchers.
Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change, which has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500. It is the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago. Scientists say that sequencing every species will revolutionise the understanding of biology and evolution, bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity.
Dr. Tim Littlewood, head of Life Sciences Department at the Natural History Museum, said, "Whether you are interested in food or disease, the history of how every organism on the planet has adapted to its environment is recorded in its genetic makeup. How you then harness that is dependent on your ability to understand it. We will be using modern methods to get a really good window on the present and the past. And of course, a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future."
Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, said, "Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project. Since 1970, humanity has wiped out 60 percent of animal populations. About 23,000 of 80,000 species surveyed are approaching extinction. We are in the midst of the sixth great extinction event of life on our planet, which not only threatens wildlife species, but also imperils the global food supply. As scientists, we all realise we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now. I think we're making history."

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century, "No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main." Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise. In his new book, The Self Delusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as "self", and not even our bodies are truly "us".
Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe, Professor Oliver said society urgently needs a Copernican-like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity. "A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the Earth is not the centre of the universe, the so-called Copernican Revolution," he writes. "However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe. You may feel as if you are an independent individual, acting autonomously in the world; that you have an unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor-point with the world changing around you. This is the illusion I seek to tackle. We are intimately connected to the world around us."
Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing. In fact, there is no part of your body that has existed for more than 10 years. "Since our bodies are essentially made anew every few weeks, the material in them alone is clearly insufficient to explain the persistent thread of an identity."
Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society, and only by realising we are part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems. Through selfish over-consumption we are destroying the natural world and using non-renewable resources at an accelerating rate. "We are at a critical crossroads as a species where we must rapidly reform our mindsets and behaviour to act in less selfish ways," he said. "So let's open our eyes to the hidden connections all around us."

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she will do?
options: Reply to the man's last proposal within a short time.
Sign the agreement if one small change is made to it.
Make a sponsorship deal for her client at the meeting.
Give the man some good news regarding the contract.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say she will do? 

 【翻译】 女士说她将做什么? 
 A)  在短时间内回复男士的最新提议。 
 B)  如果对协议做一处小的修改就签署协议。 
 C)  在会议上为她的客户达成一项赞助协议。 
 D)  告诉男士一些关于合同的好消息。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Sign the agreement if one small change is made to it. 
 【定位】 P3 W: I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract. 
 女：我确实同意了。而且我希望签署这份协议，前提是合同里做一处小改动。 

 【信号】 被问者的直接应答 + I wish to 表态 。上一句男方问 Have you agreed to my last proposal?，女方紧接着应答 I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change，这句既是被问者的直接回应，又含 I wish to 的明确表态，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 I wish to sign the agreement ↔ Sign the agreement I wish to do = 表示要做该动作 
 pending one small change to be made to the contract ↔ if one small change is made to it pending = if，都是 "先改一处为条件" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 借了男方话里的 my last proposal 拼成 Reply to the man's last proposal within a short time.，可她在 I have, indeed 里已经回复并表态要签，根本没说 "短时间内回复"，within a short time 是凭空加的。  借用原文：Have you agreed to my last proposal? 

 C) 张冠李戴 C 的 Make a sponsorship deal for her client at the meeting. 用了录音里的 make a sponsorship deal for your clients，但那是男方反问 "你到底要不要做这笔交易"，并非女方此刻 "我要做什么" 的回答；本题问的是她当下表态，答案是签约。  借用原文：Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 的 Give the man some good news regarding the contract. 盗了男方那句 please give me some good news，那是男方的请求 / 期待，女方并没说 "我要给你好消息"，她说的是愿意签约。  借用原文：please give me some good news

questions.prompt: What does the man say about some people he represents?
options: They are becoming impatient.
They are afraid time is running out.
They are used to making alterations.
They are concerned about the details.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about some people he represents? 

 【翻译】 男士关于他所代表的一些人说了什么? 
 A)  他们正变得不耐烦。 
 B)  他们担心时间不多了。 
 C)  他们习惯于做出修改。 
 D)  他们关注细节。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They are becoming impatient. 
 【定位】 P4 M: I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience. 
 男：我之所以这么问，是因为坦白说，我这边有些人快没耐心了。 

 【信号】 因果 because 后给出他对己方人员的真实描述 。他用 because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience，because 引出对 "我这边的人" 的实情描述，frankly（坦白说）更是加重语气的强调信号，这句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 running out of patience ↔ becoming impatient running out of patience = impatient，同义改写 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 的 time is running out 盗用了录音 running out of patience 里的 running out，却把宾语偷换成 time。录音里耗尽的是耐心，不是时间，B 在 running out 后面动了手脚。  借用原文：running out of patience 

 C) 答非所问 C 的 used to making alterations 取自录音 making alterations，但那是男方说双方 "这一年来回改来改去" 的背景，不是在描述 "我方那些人现在什么状态"，答非所问。  借用原文：we've been through this for almost a year now, back and forth, making alterations 

 D) 张冠李戴 D 的 concerned about the details 实际对应女方后面说的 We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts，那是女方一边推敲细节，与男方所说 "我那边的人没耐心" 是两拨人、两回事。  借用原文：We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts

questions.prompt: What reason does the woman give for the new deal to exclude the Middle East?
options: To prevent geographical discrimination.
To tap the food and beverage market.
To avoid any conflict of interest.
To reduce unfair competition.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What reason does the woman give for the new deal to exclude the Middle East? 

 【翻译】 女士给出了什么理由说明新协议要排除中东地区? 
 A)  为了防止地域歧视。 
 B)  为了开拓食品和饮料市场。 
 C)  为了避免任何利益冲突。 
 D)  为了减少不公平竞争。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） To avoid any conflict of interest. 
 【定位】 P9 W: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically. 
 女：因此，为了避免任何冲突，我们需要确保两个营销活动在地域上不重叠。 

 【信号】 in order to / therefore 双因果信号引出真目的 。她先讲客户在中东另有营销意向，再用 Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically，therefore 与 in order to 双双标出这是给理由的句子，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 in order to avoid any conflict ↔ To avoid any conflict of interest. avoid any conflict 与选项几乎原义对应 
 both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically ↔ conflict of interest 两活动地域不重叠 = 不产生利益冲突 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 的 To prevent geographical discrimination. 蹭了录音 overlap geographically 里的 geographically，造出 "地域歧视"。原文讲的是两个营销活动地域别重叠，与 "歧视" 毫不相干，是借词造假。  借用原文：both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically 

 B) 答非所问 B 的 To tap the food and beverage market. 用了录音 our food and beverage market，但那是男方在第12段说自家所属行业，与女方排除中东的理由无关；她的理由是避免冲突，不是去开发某市场。  借用原文：So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market 

 D) 未提及 D 的 To reduce unfair competition. 听着像商务套话，但录音通篇没说要减少不公平竞争，她讲的是避免客户形象在同一地域撞车的利益冲突，competition 一词原文压根没出现。

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the Middle East?
options: It is a potential market for food and beverage.
It is very attractive for real estate developers.
It is a negligible market for his company.
It is very different from other markets.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about the Middle East? 

 【翻译】 男士关于中东地区说了什么? 
 A)  它是食品和饮料的潜在市场。 
 B)  它对房地产开发商很有吸引力。 
 C)  对他的公司来说它是一个微不足道的市场。 
 D)  它与其他市场非常不同。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It is a negligible market for his company. 
 【定位】 P12 M: The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments. 
 男：中东对我们来说是个可以忽略的市场，不过我还是得跟几个部门核实一下。 

 【信号】 他对中东的直接评价句 + 形容词 negligible 。他直说 The Middle East is a negligible market for us，主系表结构直接给出评价形容词 negligible，是对中东的正面定性句，正是答案句；后半 but 起的只是补充程序，不改这句评价。 

 【替换】 a negligible market for us ↔ a negligible market for his company for us = for his company，几乎原义 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 的 It is a potential market for food and beverage. 把中东说成 "有潜力"，与他原话 a negligible market（可忽略）正好相反；food and beverage 又是蹭了他讲己方行业的熟词，双重误导。  借用原文：The Middle East is a negligible market for us 

 B) 张冠李戴 B 的 It is very attractive for real estate developers. 借了女方说的中东 Real estate，但那是女方客户在中东另有房地产营销意向，并非男方对中东市场的评价，张冠李戴。  借用原文：Real estate 

 D) 偷换概念 D 的 It is very different from other markets. 盗用了 the product is very different from our food and beverage market 里的 very different，但原文说的是 "产品" 与食饮市场不同，不是说 "中东市场" 与别的市场不同，主语被偷换。  借用原文：So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about all the astronomers at the Denver Observatory?
options: They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon.
They are celebrating a big event on mountain tops.
They are enthusiastic about big science-related stories.
They are joined by astronomers all across North America.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about all the astronomers at the Denver Observatory? 

 【翻译】 关于丹佛天文台的所有天文学家,这位女士说了什么? 
 A)  他们对一种罕见的天文现象感到兴奋。 
 B)  他们正在山顶庆祝一个重大事件。 
 C)  他们对与科学相关的重大新闻充满热情。 
 D)  北美各地的天文学家都加入了他们。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon. 
 【定位】 P2 Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited. 
 是的，在这里现场的所有天文学家都非常兴奋。 

 【信号】 被问者的直接应答 。男士在 what is the big story over there? 抛出问题，女士开口第一句 all the astronomers on site here are very excited 就是直接应答，对话题的答案落在回答方，这句即落点。 

 【替换】 all the astronomers on site here are very excited ↔ They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon. excited 同义改写为 thrilled 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 录音 congregating on mountain tops 确实念到"山顶"，但那是"聚集去观星"，不是 celebrating a big event on mountain tops 的"在山顶庆祝"，且主语是北美各地爱好者，非天文台的天文学家。  借用原文：congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky 

 C) 原词陷阱 开头 a special science-related news story 念到"科学相关"，C 项 enthusiastic about big science-related stories 直接搬这串词，但录音说的是天文学家"为这次天象兴奋"，不是"热衷各种科学新闻故事"，把对一次具体天象的兴奋偷换成对科学故事的泛泛热衷。  借用原文：a special science-related news story 

 D) 张冠李戴 录音 space enthusiasts all across North America 说的是"北美各地的爱好者要聚集"，D 项 joined by astronomers all across North America 把它改成"天文台的天文学家被北美各地天文学家加入"，主语和事件都被偷换，原文没有这层意思。  借用原文：space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the conversation about the Oppenheimer comet?
options: It will be the most formidable of its kind in over a century.
It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years.
It will eclipse many other such events in human history.
It will be seen most clearly from Denver's mountain tops.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the conversation about the Oppenheimer comet? 

 【翻译】 从对话中我们了解到关于Oppenheimer彗星的什么信息? 
 A)  它将是一个多世纪以来同类中最壮观的。 
 B)  它将在一百多年来最接近地球。 
 C)  它将使人类历史上许多其他此类事件黯然失色。 
 D)  从丹佛的山顶将最清楚地看到它。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years. 
 【定位】 P4 Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet. It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years. 
 今晚，地球将与奥本海默彗星近距离接近。这是一百多年来我们的星球离这样一种天象最近的一次。 

 【信号】 正面定性句 + 时间数字 。女士直接给彗星定性 It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years，"closest…in over 100 years" 把"距离最近"和"百年"绑在一起，是带数字的定性句，正是答案落点。 

 【替换】 the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years ↔ It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years. 主被动对调 + 数字同义 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音后文 this formidable object 确有 "formidable"，A 项 the most formidable of its kind in over a century 便把"百年"嫁接到"最厉害"上；但原文里"百年"修饰的是"距离最近"，从没说它是百年来"最厉害"的，是把数字按到了错的形容词上。  借用原文：in order to see this formidable object 

 C) 过度推断 eclipse many other such events in human history 借"eclipse"（此处作动词"使相形见绌"）和前文 Is there an eclipse happening soon? 的"日食"玩文字游戏，原文从没说这颗彗星"使人类历史上其他天象相形见绌"，属凭空拔高。  借用原文：Is there an eclipse happening soon? 

 D) 原词陷阱 seen most clearly from Denver's mountain tops 把前文 the Denver Observatory 的"丹佛"和 mountain tops 的"山顶"拼到一起，但原文只说爱好者会聚到山顶观星，从没说"从丹佛的山顶看得最清楚"，是把零散原词攒成一句没说过的话。  借用原文：congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky

questions.prompt: What does the woman say people will only see in the sky without a telescope?
options: blur.
Stars.
The edge of our galaxy.
An ordinary flying object.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say people will only see in the sky without a telescope? 

 【翻译】 这位女士说人们在没有望远镜的情况下在天空中只能看到什么? 
 A)  模糊的影像。 
 B)  星星。 
 C)  我们星系的边缘。 
 D)  一个普通的飞行物体。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） blur. 
 【定位】 P6 People will only see a blur without one. 
 没有望远镜的话，人们只会看到模糊的一团。 

 【信号】 条件 without one + only 直陈 。这句用 without one（one 指代上文 telescope）锁定"不用望远镜"的前提，再用 only see a blur 直说看到什么，前提和结果都摆明，是答案句。 

 【替换】 People will only see a blur without one ↔ blur. 原句直取，前提一致 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 录音通篇没说不用望远镜会看到"星星"，Stars. 是凭"看星空"的常识脑补出来的，原文只说看到"一团模糊"。 
 C) 原词陷阱 on the edge of our galaxy 念到"星系边缘"，但那是说彗星"所在的位置"，不是"不用望远镜看到的东西"，C 项 The edge of our galaxy. 把"它在哪"偷换成"看到什么"。  借用原文：The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy 

 D) 与原文相反 wonder at this flying object 念到 "flying object"，但那是"用普通望远镜能观赏到的彗星"，D 项 An ordinary flying object. 把它挪到"不用望远镜"的前提下——条件正好反了，不用望远镜只见模糊团，看不清是个"飞行物"。  借用原文：Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object

questions.prompt: What do scientists at the Denver Observatory advise amateurs do to facilitate their observation?
options: Use professional equipment.
Climb to the nearby heights.
Fix their eyes due north.
Make use of phone apps.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do scientists at the Denver Observatory advise amateurs do to facilitate their observation? 

 【翻译】 丹佛天文台的科学家们建议业余爱好者做什么来便于他们的观测? 
 A)  使用专业设备。 
 B)  爬到附近的高处。 
 C)  将目光固定在正北方。 
 D)  使用手机应用程序。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Make use of phone apps. 
 【定位】 P8 And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this. 
 这里的科学家告诉我，有很多手机应用程序可以帮上这个忙。 

 【信号】 建议句 + 与题干同词 facilitate 。女士转述科学家的建议 there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this，"scientists…told me"对应题干的"scientists advise"，"facilitate"与题干 facilitate their observation 同词，是答案句。 

 【替换】 there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this ↔ Make use of phone apps. 存在句 → 祈使建议 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音 that does not mean one needs professional equipment 明确说"并不需要专业设备"，A 项 Use professional equipment. 直接搬这串原词却把否定改成肯定，意思正好反了。  借用原文：that does not mean one needs professional equipment 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音 congregating on mountain tops 念到"山顶"，B 项 Climb to the nearby heights.（爬到附近高处）借此设套，但那是说爱好者去哪儿聚集，不是科学家"为方便观测给的建议"，问的根本不是同一件事。  借用原文：will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音 The comet will be almost exactly due north 念到"正北"，那是在说彗星"在天上的位置"，C 项 Fix their eyes due north. 把"它在正北方"偷换成"建议人们眼睛盯着正北"，而科学家给的方便观测的办法是用 app，不是"盯着北方"。  借用原文：The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator

questions.prompt: What question is said to have recently stirred debate?
options: Whether consumers should be warned against ultra-processed foods.
Whether there is sufficient scientific consensus on dietary guidelines.
Whether guidelines can form the basis for nutrition advice to consumers.
Whether food scientists will agree on the concept of ultra-processed foods.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What question is said to have recently stirred debate? 

 【翻译】 据说最近引发争论的问题是什么? 
 A)  是否应该警告消费者不要食用超加工食品。 
 B)  关于膳食指南是否存在充分的科学共识。 
 C)  指南能否构成向消费者提供营养建议的基础。 
 D)  食品科学家是否会就超加工食品的概念达成一致。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Whether consumers should be warned against ultra-processed foods. 
 【定位】 P1 While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods? 
 尽管围绕现有的大多数指南存在强有力的科学共识，但近来有一个问题引发了争论：是否应当警告消费者避免食用超加工食品？ 

 【信号】 冒号后正面点出争论问题 。信号是 one question has recently stirred debate: 这一句——它直接照应题干 stirred debate，而冒号之后的 should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods? 才是被点名的那个争论问题，冒号在这里起「即将给出答案」的提示作用。 

 【替换】 should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods? ↔ Whether consumers should be warned against ultra-processed foods. 疑问句→Whether名词从句，warned against=warned to avoid 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B Whether there is sufficient scientific consensus on dietary guidelines. 借用了录音里 strong scientific consensus 这个原词，但原文说的是「围绕大多数指南已存在强共识」，共识是既定背景、不是争论的问题；真正起争论的是冒号后那句，B 答非所问。  借用原文：While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines 

 C) 原词陷阱 C Whether guidelines can form the basis for nutrition advice to consumers. 几乎照搬开篇 Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice，但原文这句是肯定的陈述（指南本就是营养建议的基础），并非被拿来争论的疑问，C 把陈述句伪装成争论点。  借用原文：Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world. 

 D) 未提及 D Whether food scientists will agree on the concept of ultra-processed foods. 用了话题词 ultra-processed foods，但「食品科学家是否会就这一概念达成一致」原文根本没说——录音争论的是「要不要警告消费者」，不是「科学家认不认这个概念」，属无中生有。

questions.prompt: How does the system developed by Monteiro and colleagues classify foods?
options: By the labor cost for the final products.
By the degree of industrial processing.
By the extent of chemical alteration.
By the convention of classification.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does the system developed by Monteiro and colleagues classify foods? 

 【翻译】 Monteiro及其同事开发的系统如何对食品进行分类? 
 A)  按最终产品的人工成本。 
 B)  按工业加工程度。 
 C)  按化学改变程度。 
 D)  按分类惯例。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） By the degree of industrial processing. 
 【定位】 P3 The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed. 
 这场争论围绕蒙泰罗及其同事开发的一套系统展开，该系统按食物的工业加工程度对其分类，从未加工到超加工。 

 【信号】 专名+classifies…by 直接给出分类标准 。信号是题干专名 Monteiro 在录音里复现，紧跟的 classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing 用 classify…by… 句式正面给出分类依据，这句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 by their degree of industrial processing ↔ By the degree of industrial processing. 近乎原话对应，仅去掉物主代词 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 C By the extent of chemical alteration. 来自后一句 alter them with chemicals——但那句是在「定义什么叫超加工食品」，分类的标准是「工业加工程度」，化学改变只是超加工这一端的特征描述，不是整套系统的分类轴，C 答非所问。  借用原文：alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product 

 A) 未提及 A By the labor cost for the final products. 里 final products 蹭了原文 formulate the final product 的字眼，但「按人工成本分类」录音从没说过；原文提到的是 cheap（便宜），与「人工成本」不是一回事，属无中生有。 
 D) 与原文相反 D By the convention of classification. 借了 food classification 里的 classification 一词，但原文恰恰强调这套系统是「超越」传统分类的——第2段说要 beyond conventional food classification systems，方向正好相反，D 取了被否定的那一端。  借用原文：beyond conventional food classification systems

questions.prompt: What is consumption of ultra-processed foods linked with, according to studies?
options: Increased consumers' expenses.
Greater risk of chronic diseases.
People's misunderstanding of nutrition.
Children's dislike for unprocessed foods.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is consumption of ultra-processed foods linked with, according to studies? 

 【翻译】 根据研究,食用超加工食品与什么相关? 
 A)  消费者支出增加。 
 B)  慢性疾病风险增大。 
 C)  人们对营养的误解。 
 D)  儿童不喜欢未加工食品。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Greater risk of chronic diseases. 
 【定位】 P4 Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods—which are packed high in salt, sugar, and fat—with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet. 
 多项研究已将食用超加工食品（这类食品盐、糖、脂肪含量极高）与体重增加和慢性病风险升高联系在一起，即便在调整了膳食中盐、糖、脂肪的摄入量之后仍是如此。 

 【信号】 Studies have linked…with 正面给出关联后果 。信号是 Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods…with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases，与题干 linked with…according to studies 措辞高度对应，linked…with 后面的内容就是答案；注意中间被 salt/sugar/fat 的插入语隔开，要听完整句。 

 【替换】 an increased risk of chronic diseases ↔ Greater risk of chronic diseases. increased=greater，risk of chronic diseases 同义保留 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A Increased consumers' expenses. 蹭了第3段超加工食品 designed to be cheap 的语境联想，但原文说这类食品「便宜」，恰恰不是「让消费者花费增加」；研究关联的是健康后果，不是花钱，A 属无中生有。 
 C) 未提及 C People's misunderstanding of nutrition. 借了全文反复出现的 nutrition 话题词，但「人们对营养的误解」录音从没说过；研究关联的是体重和疾病，不是认知误解，C 无中生有。 
 D) 未提及 D Children's dislike for unprocessed foods. 用了第3段 unprocessed 一词，但「孩子不喜欢未加工食品」录音完全没提，且把话题从「健康后果」偷换成「儿童口味偏好」，属无中生有。

questions.prompt: What do psychologists say people do when they are short of resources?
options: They begin to think of the benefits of constraints.
They try to seek solutions from creative people.
They try hard to maximize their mental energy.
They begin to see the world in a different way.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do psychologists say people do when they are short of resources? 

 【翻译】 心理学家说,当人们资源短缺时会做什么? 
 A)  他们开始思考约束的好处。 
 B)  他们试图从有创造力的人那里寻求解决方案。 
 C)  他们努力最大化自己的心理能量。 
 D)  他们开始以不同的方式看待世界。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They begin to see the world in a different way. 
 【定位】 P1 According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently. 
 据心理学家所说，当你可支配的东西更少时，你实际上会开始用不同的方式看待世界。 

 【信号】 题干信号词 psychologists 顺听定位 。题干问的是 psychologists（心理学家）的说法，录音里恰有 According to psychologists 这一引述信号，紧跟其后的 you actually begin to see the world differently 就是答案句；篇章题题目多与录音同序，听到 psychologists 就知道答案落在它后面那句。 

 【替换】 begin to see the world differently ↔ begin to see the world in a different way 副词换介词短语 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 用了全文话题词 constraints，但 think of the benefits of constraints（想到约束的好处）是录音从未说过的动作，录音说的是人开始换个方式看世界，A 只是借 constraints 这个耳熟的词诱你误选。  借用原文：human creativity benefits from constraints 

 B) 未提及 B 说人去 seek solutions from creative people（向有创造力的人求解），录音通篇讲的是人自己换方式看世界、自己更灵活地用资源，从没说去向别人求助，属无中生有。 
 C) 原词陷阱 C 出现 maximize their mental energy，录音确有 dedicate your mental energy（投入心智能量）这个词，但原文说的是把心智能量投入到更灵活地行动，不是 maximize（最大化）能量本身，C 盗用 mental energy 这个原词却篡改了它的动作。  借用原文：you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about innovation?
options: It is characteristic of all creative people.
It is essential to pushing society forward.
It is a creative person's response to limitation.
It is an impetus to socio-economic development.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about innovation? 

 【翻译】 文章关于创新说了什么? 
 A)  这是所有有创造力的人的特征。 
 B)  这对推动社会前进至关重要。 
 C)  这是有创造力的人对限制的回应。 
 D)  这是社会经济发展的推动力。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It is a creative person's response to limitation. 
 【定位】 P3 Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation. 
 创新是有创造力的人对限制做出的回应。 

 【信号】 段首定性句直接定义 。第三段开头 Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation. 是一句标准的 X is Y 定性句，主语正是题干的 innovation；篇章题里这种段首主语直接成句的定义往往就是答案句，听到 Innovation is 就该锁定。 

 【替换】 a creative person's response to limitation ↔ a creative person's response to limitation 罕见的近乎原句对应 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 A 说创新 characteristic of all creative people（所有有创造力的人的特征），录音说的是创新是有创造力者对限制的回应，并没有断言它是所有这类人都具备的特征，all 把范围说死，属偷换概念。  借用原文：The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher. 

 B) 过度推断 B 说创新 essential to pushing society forward（对推动社会前进至关重要），录音有 impetus（推动力）一词，但说的是约束给人的头脑以跃升的推动力，并非创新对推动社会前进必不可少，B 把对象偷偷拔高到社会层面，过度推断。  借用原文：constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 说创新是 impetus to socio-economic development（社会经济发展的推动力），impetus 虽是原词，但 socio-economic development（社会经济发展）录音从头到尾没提，纯属拿原词拼接出一个原文没有的结论。  借用原文：constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher

questions.prompt: What did a 2015 study by Ravi Mehta and Meng Zhu find?
options: Scarcity or abundance of resources has little impact on people's creativity.
Innovative people are not constrained in connecting unrelated concepts.
People have no incentive to use available resources in new ways.
Creative people tend to consume more available resources.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did a 2015 study by Ravi Mehta and Meng Zhu find? 

 【翻译】 Ravi Mehta和Meng Zhu在2015年的研究中发现了什么? 
 A)  资源的稀缺或充裕对人们的创造力影响很小。 
 B)  创新型人才在连接不相关概念时不受约束。 
 C)  人们没有动力以新方式使用可用资源。 
 D)  有创造力的人往往会消耗更多可用资源。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） People have no incentive to use available resources in new ways. 
 【定位】 P3 Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways. 
 伊利诺伊大学的拉维·梅塔和约翰·霍普金斯大学的朱萌发现，人们根本没有动力以新颖的方式使用手头现有的东西。 

 【信号】 人名加 found that 引出发现 。录音里 Ravi Mehta 与 Meng Zhu 两个人名后紧跟 found that，这是研究发现的标志信号，that 引导的从句就是答案内容；听到人名加 found that，答案句必在其后。 

 【替换】 no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways ↔ no incentive to use available resources in new ways 近义词逐处替换 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 说 Scarcity or abundance of resources has little impact on people's creativity（资源稀缺或充裕对创造力影响不大），录音确实研究了 scarcity or abundance 如何影响创造性用资源，但结论恰恰是影响很大、稀缺反而激发创造，A 把研究的对象词盗来却得出与原文相反的结论。  借用原文：how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources 

 B) 答非所问 B 说 Innovative people are not constrained in connecting unrelated concepts（创新者在联结不相关概念时不受约束），录音末句确有 connecting unrelated ideas and concepts 这个搭配，但那是说持续的约束帮助人更善于联结不相关概念，并非这项 2015 研究的发现，B 把别处的原词搬到研究结论上，答非所问。  借用原文：Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts. 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 说 Creative people tend to consume more available resources（有创造力的人倾向消耗更多现有资源），available resources 蹭了原文的词，但 consume more（消耗更多）录音从未提及，录音讲的是以新方式使用资源，不是消耗更多，纯属编造。  借用原文：use what's available to them in novel ways

questions.prompt: What did Marissa Mayer once write concerning creativity?
options: It is key to a company's survival.
It shapes and focuses problems.
It is essential to meeting challenges
It thrives best when constrained.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Marissa Mayer once write concerning creativity? 

 【翻译】 Marissa Mayer曾就创造力写过什么? 
 A)  这是公司生存的关键。 
 B)  它塑造并聚焦问题。 
 C)  它对应对挑战至关重要。 
 D)  它在受到约束时最为繁荣。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It thrives best when constrained. 
 【定位】 P4 Constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome; Creativity thrives best when constrained. 
 约束塑造并聚焦问题，并提供明确的、需要去克服的挑战；创造力在受约束时最为繁盛。 

 【信号】 题干限定词 creativity 锁后半句 。Mayer 的引述有前后两句，前半 Constraints shape and focus problems 主语是约束，后半 Creativity thrives best when constrained 主语才是 creativity；题干限定 concerning creativity，信号就是这个限定词，答案锁后半句。 

 【替换】 Creativity thrives best when constrained ↔ It thrives best when constrained. 代词 It 回指 creativity 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 说创造力 key to a company's survival（对公司生存至关重要），虽然录音提到 Mayer 曾是 Google 的副总裁，但她写的话里根本没提公司生存，A 凭 Google 这一职务背景臆造出公司话题，属未提及。 
 B) 张冠李戴 B 说 It shapes and focuses problems.，这句确实摘自 Mayer 的话 Constraints shape and focus problems，但原文该动作的主语是 Constraints（约束）不是 creativity，题干问的是关于 creativity 的内容，B 把约束做的事安到了创造力头上，主语张冠李戴。  借用原文：Constraints shape and focus problems 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 说创造力 essential to meeting challenges（对应对挑战至关重要），录音里 challenges 一词出自 provide clear challenges to overcome，说的是约束提供需克服的挑战，而非创造力对应对挑战必不可少，C 盗用 challenges 偷换了逻辑关系。  借用原文：provide clear challenges to overcome

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say strategies for managing conflicts can always be changed?
options: Because they are learned.
Because they come naturally.
Because they have to be properly personalized.
Because there can be more effective strategies.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the speaker say strategies for managing conflicts can always be changed? 

 【翻译】 为什么说话者说管理冲突的策略总是可以改变的? 
 A)  因为它们是习得的。 
 B)  因为它们是自然而然产生的。 
 C)  因为它们必须被适当地个性化。 
 D)  因为可能存在更有效的策略。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Because they are learned. 
 【定位】 P1 But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts. 
 但我们确实有一套个人策略，而正因为它是后天习得的，我们总能通过学习新的、更有效的冲突处理方式来改变它。 

 【信号】 because 直接交代原因 。这句里 because it is learned, we can always change it 是赤裸裸的因果结构："because + 原因"紧跟着"can always change"。原因题听到 because 就锁这句，不必再听后文。 

 【替换】 because it is learned ↔ Because they are learned. 几乎原句搬到选项 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音确实说过 We just do whatever seems to come naturally，但那是讲"我们平时不自觉、顺其自然地行事"，并非"策略能被改变的原因"。B 把这个原词搬来当原因，恰恰用反了——天生自然反而是难改的那一面。  借用原文：We just do whatever seems to come naturally 

 C) 偷换概念 录音提到策略是 a personal strategy（个人的），C 顺势造出 they have to be properly personalized（必须妥善个性化）。但录音从没说"必须被个性化"是它能改变的原因，这是把"个人的"偷换成"必须个性化"的无中生有。  借用原文：a personal strategy 

 D) 答非所问 录音末尾确有 more effective ways，D 据此说 there can be more effective strategies。但"有更有效的策略"在录音里是"改变之后能达到的效果/途径"，不是"能改变"的原因；真正的原因是它习得（learned）。D 把结果当成了原因。  借用原文：more effective ways of managing conflicts

questions.prompt: What is said to affect the way one acts in a conflict?
options: The extent of difference and of similarity between the two sides.
The knowledge of the specific expectation the other side holds.
The importance of one's goals and of the relationship.
The approaches one adopts to conflict management.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is said to affect the way one acts in a conflict? 

 【翻译】 什么被认为会影响一个人在冲突中的行为方式? 
 A)  双方之间差异和相似的程度。 
 B)  对另一方所持特定期望的了解。 
 C)  一个人的目标和关系的重要性。 
 D)  一个人采用的冲突管理方法。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The importance of one's goals and of the relationship. 
 【定位】 P1 How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict. 
 你的个人目标有多重要、以及这段关系对你有多重要，这两点影响你在冲突中如何行事。 

 【信号】 原句直接出现 affect 。这句的主干就是 How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act，动词 affect 与题干 affect 同词出现，谓语前的两个主语（目标重要性、关系重要性）即所求，是教科书式的"信号词同词复现"定位点。 

 【替换】 How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you ↔ The importance of one's goals and of the relationship. 句子改名词化 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 说 The extent of difference and of similarity between the two sides.（双方差异与相似的程度）听上去很学术，但录音通篇没说"差异/相似程度"会影响行为。这是凭"冲突=双方有分歧"的常识脑补出来的，原文无据。 
 B) 原词陷阱 B 说 The knowledge of the specific expectation the other side holds.（了解对方的具体期待）。录音确实反复说到"the other person"，但从没说"知道对方期待什么"会影响你的行为，影响行为的是你自己目标和关系的重要性。B 借了"对方"这个原词，却安了个录音没说的内容。  借用原文：keeping a good relationship with the other person 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 说 The approaches one adopts to conflict management.（处理冲突所采取的方法）。这正是整篇的大主题词 managing conflicts，但题目问的是"什么影响你的做法"，而"做法本身"不能影响"做法"，逻辑上自指。D 盗用了贯穿全文的话题词来冒充答案。  借用原文：strategies for managing conflicts

questions.prompt: Of the five styles the speaker discusses, which views conflicts as problems to be solved?
options: The fox.
The owl.
The shark.
The turtle.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Of the five styles the speaker discusses, which views conflicts as problems to be solved? 

 【翻译】 在说话者讨论的五种风格中,哪一种将冲突视为需要解决的问题? 
 A)  狐狸型。 
 B)  猫头鹰型。 
 C)  鲨鱼型。 
 D)  乌龟型。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） The owl. 
 【定位】 P6 The owl. Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved. 
 猫头鹰。猫头鹰把冲突视为有待解决的问题。 

 【信号】 原句逐字复述特征 。第 6 段开头先报名字 The owl，紧接着 Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved 与题干 views conflicts as problems to be solved 几乎一字不差。匹配题里，题干特征在哪段被原样念出，那段的主角就是答案。 

 【替换】 Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved ↔ The owl. 特征绑定到名字 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 A 是 The fox.。狐狸的特征是 both sides gain something（双方各让一步、各得一点），属于折中妥协，录音没说狐狸"把冲突看作待解决的问题"。它和 owl 都偏正面，最易混，但定性不同。  借用原文：They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something. 

 C) 与原文相反 C 是 The shark.。鲨鱼的特征是 overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution（强压对方、逼其接受），与"把冲突当问题来解决"正相反。鲨鱼追求一方赢一方输，绝非协商解决。  借用原文：Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution 

 D) 与原文相反 D 是 The turtle.。乌龟的特征是 withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts（缩进壳里逃避冲突），它连面对都不愿意，更谈不上"把冲突当问题来解决"，与题干特征截然相反。  借用原文：Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts.

questions.prompt: What do scientists hope to do by cracking the genetic code of plants and animals?
options: Help save species from extinction and boost human health.
Understand how plants and animals perished over the past.
Help gather information publicly available to researchers.
Find out the cause of extinction of Britain's 66, 000 species.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do scientists hope to do by cracking the genetic code of plants and animals? 

 【翻译】 科学家希望通过破解动植物的遗传密码来做什么? 
 A)  帮助拯救物种免于灭绝并促进人类健康。 
 B)  了解动植物在过去是如何灭亡的。 
 C)  帮助收集研究人员可公开获取的信息。 
 D)  找出英国66000个物种灭绝的原因。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Help save species from extinction and boost human health. 
 【定位】 P1 The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health. 
 地球上全部 150 万已知动植物物种的基因密码都将被绘制出来，以帮助拯救物种免于灭绝、并提升人类健康。 

 【信号】 目的信号 to help 后面接落点 。答案句靠目的状语 to help save species from extinction and boost human health 中的 to help 锁定——"做基因测序"的目的正写在 to help 之后，这正是题干 hope to do 要的那一层。 

 【替换】 save species from extinction and boost human health ↔ Help save species from extinction and boost human health. 选项几乎原句搬来，只在前面加 Help 

 【排除】 B) 答非所问 本项 Understand how plants and animals perished over the past. 借了"动植物消亡"的料（呼应录音第 3 段大量物种灭绝的描述），但说的是"理解过去它们如何消亡"，而录音目的是"拯救现在的物种"，把"救（未来）"偷换成"懂（过去）"，答非所问。  借用原文：has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500 

 C) 原词陷阱 Help gather information publicly available to researchers. 直接搬了录音 all the information will be publicly available to researchers，但那是说"项目完成后信息将公开给研究者"，是项目的副产品，不是"破解基因码"这一动作的目的，典型原词陷阱。  借用原文：all the information will be publicly available to researchers 

 D) 原词陷阱 Find out the cause of extinction of Britain's 66, 000 species. 搬了录音 Britain's 66,000 species 这个醒目数字，又拼上"找灭绝原因"，但录音从没说目的是"查灭绝原因"，且 66,000 是英国测序的物种数、与"破解基因码的目的"是两码事，原词＋无中生有。  借用原文：Britain's 66,000 species of animals and plants

questions.prompt: What do many scientists believe with regard to earth?
options: It was once dominated by dinosaurs.
It has entered the sixth mass extinction.
Its prospects depend on future human behaviour.
Its climate change is aggravated by humans.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do many scientists believe with regard to earth? 

 【翻译】 许多科学家对地球持什么看法? 
 A)  它曾经由恐龙统治。 
 B)  它已进入第六次大灭绝。 
 C)  它的前景取决于人类未来的行为。 
 D)  它的气候变化因人类而加剧。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It has entered the sixth mass extinction. 
 【定位】 P3 Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change. 
 许多科学家相信，地球如今已进入第六次大规模物种灭绝，人类制造出栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化交织而成的有毒组合。 

 【信号】 观点信号 Many scientists believe 直接引出 。答案句由 Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction 这个观点引导句锁定——题干 believe 与原文 believe 对齐，believe 后的 that 从句就是"许多科学家相信什么"的答案。 

 【替换】 earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction ↔ It has entered the sixth mass extinction. earth→It，其余原句保留 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It was once dominated by dinosaurs. 蹭录音里的 dinosaurs，但原文说的是 the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago——恐龙是被灭绝来做"损失之大"的参照，录音从没说"地球曾被恐龙统治"，纯属听到 dinosaurs 就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago 

 C) 偷换概念 Its prospects depend on future human behaviour. 说"地球前景取决于未来人类行为"，录音第 4 段虽提到 a window on the future，但那是讲项目能模型化未来，并非"许多科学家相信地球前景取决于人类未来行为"，把别处的零碎拼成新断言，无中生有。  借用原文：a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future 

 D) 原词陷阱 Its climate change is aggravated by humans. 抓住录音 habitat loss, pollution and climate change 里的 climate change 单独放大，但原文是"栖息地丧失、污染、气候变化"三者并列、共同构成有毒组合，单拎一项当作"科学家相信地球如何"，以偏概全。  借用原文：a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change

questions.prompt: How does Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, describe the Darwin Tree of Life Project?
options: It dwarfs all other efforts to conserve, protect and restore biodiversity on earth.
It is costly to get started and requires the joint efforts of thousands of scientists.
It can help to bring back the large numbers of plants and animals that have gone extinct.
It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, describe the Darwin Tree of Life Project? 

 【翻译】 Wellcome科学主任Jim Smith爵士如何描述生命之树计划? 
 A)  它使地球上所有其他保护、保护和恢复生物多样性的努力都相形见绌。 
 B)  它启动成本高昂,需要数千名科学家的共同努力。 
 C)  它可以帮助恢复已经灭绝的大量动植物。 
 D)  它是最激动人心、最相关、最及时和最具国际启发性的。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational. 
 【定位】 P5 Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, said, "Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project." 
 Wellcome 科学总监 Jim Smith 爵士说："无论我怎么想，都想不出还有比这更激动人心、更切题、更及时、更具国际启发性的项目。" 

 【信号】 评价语气：I can't think of a more… 是变相最高级 。答案句靠 I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project 这个"想不出更…的"否定结构锁定——"想不出比它更…的"等于"它是最…的"，是说话人对项目的最高评价。 

 【替换】 I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project ↔ It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational. "想不出更…的"="最…的"，比较级转最高级 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It dwarfs all other efforts to conserve, protect and restore biodiversity on earth. 蹭了录音 conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity 的原词，但说"它使其它一切保护努力相形见绌"是录音没有的比较，且这是 Jim Smith 的评价题，A 拼的是别处第 3 段的料，张冠李戴。  借用原文：bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity 

 B) 答非所问 It is costly to get started and requires the joint efforts of thousands of scientists. 蹭了录音 cost £100 million 与众多科学家协作的料，但这是讲项目的成本与规模，是客观事实，不是 Jim Smith"如何形容/评价"项目，答非所问。  借用原文：it is expected to take 10 years and cost £100 million 

 C) 过度推断 It can help to bring back the large numbers of plants and animals that have gone extinct. 用了录音常出现的"动植物灭绝"原词，但录音只说项目能助保护、记录生命，从没说能"把已灭绝物种带回来"，明显过度推断。  借用原文：we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now

questions.prompt: What is indeed just an illusion according to Professor Tom Oliver?
options: Cultural identity.
Social evolution.
The Copernican revolution.
Human individuality.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is indeed just an illusion according to Professor Tom Oliver? 

 【翻译】 根据Tom Oliver教授的观点,什么实际上只是一种幻觉? 
 A)  文化身份。 
 B)  社会演化。 
 C)  哥白尼革命。 
 D)  人类个体性。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Human individuality. 
 【定位】 P1 Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise. 
 如今，一位英国学者声称，人的个体独立性其实只是一种幻觉，因为社会在心理、生理和文化层面上的相互联系远比人们意识到的紧密。 

 【信号】 原句直陈定性 。答案句直接用 human individuality is indeed just an illusion 把某概念点定为"幻觉"，is just an illusion 这种判定句就是信号，听到"X 其实只是个幻觉"就锁定 X。 

 【替换】 human individuality ↔ Human individuality. 原词直接对应 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 The Copernican revolution. 盗用了录音第二段反复出现的 Copernican，但哥白尼革命是讲者用来作类比的"参照"，不是被称为幻觉的对象，属听到 Copernican 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：the so-called Copernican Revolution 

 B) 原词陷阱 Social evolution. 借了录音 the cultural evolution of human minds 里的 evolution 一词，但"社会／文化演化"是讲者描述心智发展的背景，并未被定性为幻觉。  借用原文：A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds 

 A) 偷换概念 Cultural identity. 与录音 cultural level 的 cultural 沾边，但讲者说的是"文化层面的联系"，从未把"文化身份"称为幻觉，属偷换概念。  借用原文：at a mental, physical, and cultural level

questions.prompt: What does Professor Tom Oliver think of the idea that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe?
options: It is a delusion to be disposed of.
It is prevalent even among academics.
It is a myth spread by John Donne's poem.
It is rooted in the mindset of the 17th century.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does Professor Tom Oliver think of the idea that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe? 

 【翻译】 Tom Oliver教授如何看待我们作为独立自我存在于主观宇宙中心这一观念? 
 A)  这是一种应当被摒弃的错觉。 
 B)  即使在学术界这种观念也很普遍。 
 C)  这是一个由John Donne的诗歌传播的谬误。 
 D)  这根植于17世纪的思维模式。 

 【答案】 A （态度观点题） It is a delusion to be disposed of. 
 【定位】 P2 However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe. 
 然而，我们还有一个大迷思需要破除：即我们以为自己是独立的自我、处在一个主观宇宙的中心。 

 【信号】 转折However后是真意 。句首 However 转折之后才是讲者真正要表达的态度，他把那个想法称为 one more big myth to dispose of（又一个要破除的迷思），处置动词 dispose of 直接给出否定态度。 

 【替换】 one more big myth to dispose of ↔ a delusion to be disposed of myth=delusion同义替换 

 【排除】 D) 原词陷阱 rooted in the mindset of the 17th century 盗用了录音开头 wrote in the 17th century 的时间词，但 17 世纪说的是 John Donne 写诗的年代，讲者从未说那个"独立自我"的想法植根于 17 世纪心态，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：wrote in the 17th century 

 C) 张冠李戴 a myth spread by John Donne's poem 把"迷思"归因到 John Donne 的诗，盗用了开头出现的 John Donne，但讲者引 Donne 的诗恰恰是支持"人互相连接"，并非说这首诗散布了迷思，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main 

 B) 未提及 prevalent even among academics（连学者中都很普遍）原文从未提及，讲者只说这是普遍的 illusion，没有专门强调"在学者中尤其普遍"，属未提及。

questions.prompt: Why does Professor Tom Oliver claim that the material "us" is constantly changing?
options: He believes in Copernican philosophical doctrines about the universe.
He has gained ample scientific evidence at the University of Reading.
He has found that our inner self and material self are interconnected.
He contends most of our body cells can only live a few days or weeks.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does Professor Tom Oliver claim that the material "us" is constantly changing? 

 【翻译】 为什么Tom Oliver教授声称物质层面的"我们"在不断变化? 
 A)  他信奉哥白尼关于宇宙的哲学学说。 
 B)  他在Reading大学获得了充分的科学证据。 
 C)  他发现我们的内在自我与物质自我是相互关联的。 
 D)  他认为我们身体的大部分细胞只能存活几天或几周。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） He contends most of our body cells can only live a few days or weeks. 
 【定位】 P3 Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing. 
 奥利弗教授指出，人体内约有37万亿个细胞，但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周，因此物质意义上的"我们"在不断变化。
